facility.name: Lake Highlands Presbyterian Cdc

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver failed to supervise children when they exited the classroom, leaving several children without an actively supervising caregiver for about two minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers: A caregiver failed to share necessary information with an incoming caregiver by exiting the classroom without clearly communicating that they were leaving and without confirming that the incoming caregiver had assumed responsibility for the children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers (26 TAC §746.1203(10))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to timely report allegations of possible mistreatment of children to Child Care Regulation after management became aware of the concerns.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: It was determined that a caregiver used prohibited physical punishment by grabbing and pulling a child by one arm.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: During an investigation, it was determined that a caregiver used inappropriate verbal discipline by yelling at children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: I observed an infant sitting in a bouncer without being properly strapped in Infant A.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver in room 109 fell asleep while caring for children.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found to be deficient.  The operation has not yet received parent signature on the incident report to indicate the report had been shared with the child's parents.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found to be deficient. A child with a diagnosed food allergy was given a food item that contained three of the child?s identified allergens. Resulting in allergic reaction requiring medical treatment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child (26 TAC §746.3301(i))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found to be deficient. A caregiver demonstrated poor judgement and competency after failing to follow allergy protocols and giving a child with diagnosed food allergen a food item without getting authorization from the child?s parent or reading the label to ensure it did not contain the child?s allergens.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: During an infant class observation, an infant was found not properly strapped into a child bouncer. This was corrected during the inspection after the caregiver strapped the child in.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: During a classroom transition, a child was left unattended.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: A caregiver inappropriately redirected a child during nap by hitting their leg.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. Two caregivers transitioning a group of children outside did not ensure all children were accounted for before leaving the classroom. As a result, one child was left unattended in the classroom restroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A caregiver fed the wrong bottle to an infant.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A caregiver departing their classroom did not relay classroom information to the incoming caregiver, resulting in uncertainty about who was responsible for the group. This led to the classroom being left unattended for at least five minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers (26 TAC §746.1203(10))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A classroom was left unattended for at least five minutes due to a miscommunication between caregivers.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less: Loose fill under two playground structures does not meet a depth of at least six inches.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Installation and Maintenance of Loose-fill Surfacing - Six Inches if Equipment 5 Ft or Less (26 TAC §746.4907(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A caregiver gave one child the wrong infant bottle.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: Five of the seven food allergy emergency plans do not have parent signatures.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)

occurrences.finding: Posting Requirements - Child's Food Allergy Plans: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A child's food allergy was not posted in their classroom by the child's first day in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Posting Requirements - Child's Food Allergy Plans (26 TAC §746.403(b))

occurrences.finding: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. A child was served food identified on their food allergy emergency plan.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Nutrition and Food Service - Must not serve identified foods to allergic child (26 TAC §746.3301(i))

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: 3 classrooms were checked, and found to have cots the did not have a child's name on the cot or label with a number to match a child's name assignment map available.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A caregiver left 2 children unsupervised in the bathroom. After a minute the caregiver looked in the bathroom to monitor the children,
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: Caregivers in the operation left a child unattended in the classroom. The administrative staff found the child in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance: The operation did not have a procedure in place to account for the number of children that transitioned from one area of the operation to another.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Director Responsibilities - Operate in Compliance (26 TAC §746.1003(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - Arranged for Supervision: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient. Indoor furniture was arranged in a way that did not allow for caregivers to properly supervise.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - Arranged for Supervision (26 TAC §746.4601(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering: One caregiver was observed not washing a child's hands after diaper changing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Handwashing After Toileting or Diapering (26 TAC §746.3417(3))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Caregiver's Hands Washed: In two classrooms, caregiver's hands were not washed after diaper changing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Caregiver's Hands Washed (26 TAC §746.3505(a))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area: Diaper changing tables are not sanitized according to the manufacturer instructions. The diaper changing surface is to be sprayed and set for one minute before wiping to be sanitized. Caregivers were not waiting the full minute to wipe down the table.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area (26 TAC §746.3505(e))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Designated Location Inside: The emergency evacuation diagram does not indicate the location inside thte center where children and caregivers shelter in place.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Designated Location Inside (26 TAC §746.5207(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: One child with diagnosed food allergy had an incomplete food allergy plan. The plan did not specify each food the child is allergic to, it did not list possible symptoms if the child is exposed to the food, steps to take if a child has an allergic reaction, and it was not signed by the parent.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §746.3819)

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: A child with a food allergy indicated by the physician consumed food they were allergic to. This child experienced allergic reaction symptoms. This information was not reported to CCR.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Wash Infant's Hands: In two classrooms, infant's hands were not washed after diaper changing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Wash Infant's Hands (26 TAC §746.3505(b))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR: One caregiver that has worked at the operation for at least 90 days is not current in CPR training.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric CPR (26 TAC §746.1315(b))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Designated Location: The designated relocation site was not indicate on the emergency evacuation diagrams.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Evacuation and Relocation Diagram - Designated Location (26 TAC §746.5207(a)(3))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual: This standard was tasked as part of an investigation and found deficient.   Inappropriate guidance was used by a caregiver when redirecting a child's behavior. The   caregiver picked a child up by their legs and flipped them onto their stomach during naptime.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - No Harsh, Cruel or Unusual (26 TAC §746.2805)

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was in deficient. Bleach was inside a bubble bottle that was not labeled correctly.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was in deficient. A child gained access to a hazardous material and spilled it on their clothes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials (26 TAC §746.3407(13))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was in deficient. The caregivers did not know the group of children they were responsible for.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know children responsible for (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(1))

occurrences.finding: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps: An infant was observed not being strapped in while sitting at a kidney feeding table. This was corrected during the inspection the infant was removed from table.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Infant Care Area Furnishings and Equipment -Use of Safety Straps (26 TAC §746.2407)

occurrences.finding: Children's Products-Posting of CPSC website: The operation did not have updated documentation for CPSC recall items. This was corrected during inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products-Posting of CPSC website (26 TAC §746.4135(c))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: An infant feeding instruction reviewed had not been updated within the required timeframe.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was deficient.  Children were being yelled at and humiliated.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Humiliating, Rejecting, Yelling (26 TAC §746.2805(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was deficient.  A caregiver aggressively placed a child on their nap mat. It was also determined that a caregiver applied pressure with her arm on a child chest during diaper changing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk: The operation failed to notify childcare regulation within the required timeframe when they were made aware of a situation that placed children at risk.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Situation Placing Children at Risk (26 TAC §746.305(a)(6))

occurrences.finding: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits: One child was blocking the classrooms entrance during naptime. The child was moved to another part of the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Arrangement of Napping Equipment - Not Blocking Entrances or Exits (26 TAC §746.2909(1))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional: Ten  infant schedules were reviewed and did not have the required signature. Three of ten infant schedules reviewed did not have the required date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Signed and Dated by Parent or Health-Care Professional (26 TAC §746.2421(a))
